assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new classification of electronic phases of matter, grounded in band theory that can be computed from first principles and tied to measurable edge states and surface spectra. It has reshaped condensed-matter physics and spawned topological photonics, magnetism and superconductivity. It is a clean, verified physical discovery with a theory-to-experiment arc, which is what I look for.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 classification and quantum spin Hall prediction for graphene; Molenkamp's group made the decisive HgTe/CdTe edge-transport observation, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. A theory-plus-experiment trio is natural, but the prediction of the HgTe route is not covered by the supplied names, and 3D topological insulator ARPES work (Hasan, Hsieh and others) is also not covered.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: nearly two decades of independent confirmation across many materials and laboratories (transport, ARPES, STM), and a stable interpretation. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with the BHZ proposal and with 3D topological insulator discoveries outside the supplied names.
Whether the committee prefers to pair this with the quantum anomalous Hall effect or treat B004 as a competing framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created a tunable platform where flat bands give correlated insulators and superconductivity, a new quantum-material paradigm that has launched moire physics. The discovery of unexpected superconductivity in a simple carbon system is exactly the kind of surprise from quantum mechanics that matters to the field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group (with Cao as lead author) observed the correlated and superconducting states. All three credited names are plausible, but I would propose MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero to respect the three-person limit and the theory/experiment pairing. Bistritzer's share and the roles of early contributors and the experimental junior authors are unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Roughly eight years old and independently reproduced by many groups with expanding phenomenology, but the nature of the superconductivity and the sample-to-sample variability are still debated, so the interpretation is not fully settled.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Reproducibility across devices depends on twist-angle disorder and strain.
Allocation between Bistritzer and MacDonald, and earlier flat-band theory work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory became the standard framework for strongly correlated electrons, explaining the Mott transition and, combined with DFT, yielding quantitative spectra of correlated materials. Its originality and lasting impact on computational materials theory are substantial and directly connected to my own field, where DFT+DMFT is used to interpret photoemission and other spectra.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt's infinite-dimension limit (1989), Georges and Kotliar's mapping to an impurity problem (1992), and Georges, Kotliar, Krauth and Rozenberg's review form the core. Muller-Hartmann and Metzner also contributed to the foundations, and Krauth and Rozenberg are not in the supplied names, so a three-person award would leave out real contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than three decades of use and refinement, extensive agreement with spectroscopy, and mainstream status. Quantitative predictivity for real materials is still method- and implementation-dependent.
uncertainties: Prize-fit for a method versus a discovery.
Cross-code reproducibility of DFT+DMFT for real materials is weaker than for plain DFT.
Fair allocation among Metzner, Muller-Hartmann, Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance turned spin-dependent tunnelling into a practical effect and underlies read heads and magnetic memory. It is a clear experimental discovery with a physical explanation in terms of spin-polarized band structure, and with large technological reach. The 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance sets a precedent and also raises the question of whether this is sufficiently distinct.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin and, separately, Yuasa and colleagues established giant MgO-based TMR in 2004. The supplied names cover a plausible trio but Yuasa and Djayaprawira are excluded, so credit for the MgO step is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed and in commercial use for two decades. Timing is ample, if anything late.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may count against it.
Credit for the MgO barrier breakthrough is not fully captured by the supplied names.
Julliere's earlier low-temperature work is not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-resolution ARPES gave direct access to the electronic structure of cuprates and other correlated materials, including Fermi surfaces, pseudogaps and kinks, and so enabled a generation of theory-experiment comparisons. It is a measurement capability that created discoveries, rather than a single discovery, which I weigh carefully.
assessment.attribution: Campuzano and Shen are the leading pioneers in cuprate ARPES, but Spicer, Plummer, Hufner, Dessau and instrument developers like Damascelli, Hufner and the Tokyo group also contributed. A two-person award is possible but the boundaries of the method are blurry.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, though the scientific payoff for cuprate pairing remains unresolved, which makes the framing as a discovery uncertain.
uncertainties: Instrument and technique versus discovery framing.
Who is decisive among a large community of ARPES developers.
The cuprate mechanism remains open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third basic class of collinear magnet with zero net magnetization but spin-split bands, a conceptually clear result in my own area that connects symmetry, first-principles band structure and measurable spectroscopy. It has strong potential for spintronics.
assessment.attribution: Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth formulated the symmetry classification and the spin-group framework, and earlier materials and observations (e.g. in MnTe, CrSb) by other groups exist. The three names are a coherent theory trio, though the experimental confirmers are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Premature: the classification dates from 2022 and ARPES and other confirmations from 2024 are recent and the technological impact is not established. I would rank it highly in the next several cycles rather than now.
uncertainties: Limited independent confirmation history so far.
Earlier related work on spin-split antiferromagnets may affect priority.
Technological relevance is projected, not demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum computer and, with others, the framework for quantum simulation with cold atoms. This theory enabled whole experimental fields and ties well to the idea that quantum mechanics keeps delivering new capabilities. It is strong, but outside my core expertise, so I defer on fine detail.
assessment.attribution: The two names form a clean and widely recognized theory pair, but the optical-lattice simulation side also involves Jaksch, Bloch, Greiner and others, and the trapped-ion experiments of Wineland and Blatt were already recognized in part by the 2012 prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature in theory with extensive experimental realization, though a fault-tolerant ion-trap computer is not yet a reality.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2012 Nobel Prize and the competing B010 and B028 framings.
I lack deep expertise in AMO attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Current-induced spin-transfer torque allows magnetization to be switched and driven by electrical current, which is the basis of STT-MRAM and also links directly to atomistic spin dynamics theory. It is a combined theory-and-experiment story with practical sustainability angles in non-volatile memory.
assessment.attribution: Berger and Slonczewski predicted the effect in 1996; Slonczewski is not among the supplied names and Berger is deceased, which complicates any prize configuration. Ralph and Buhrman demonstrated it experimentally, but the theory half is not fully represented by the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, with commercial devices. Timing is reasonable, but the allocation problem is serious.
uncertainties: Slonczewski is missing and Berger is deceased, so theory credit cannot be fairly allocated.
Overlap with the earlier GMR prize.
